title: Journey - Five Days of Peace - Day 4: Daily bread

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Peace. <short pause> This is day four, Daily Bread. <short pause> We have three steps now. <short pause> Here it is. <short pause> It's Yours. <short pause> Help me, and thank You. <short pause> Today we make the worry smaller... by making it only as wide as one day.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Take a moment to find today. <short pause> What can you hear in it? <short pause> What is the light like, where you are? <short pause> Let your body be here, at this hour, and at no other. <short pause> Breathe in the air of this day... <short pause> and let it out.

So much of what exhausts us hasn't happened yet. <short pause> We attend next week's appointment a dozen times. <short pause> We have next month's argument in the shower. <short pause> We try to live all of those days with the strength that was given for this one. <short pause> No wonder we are tired. <short pause> One person was never meant to live a whole year at once.

Jesus once told a worried crowd to look up at the birds. <short pause> They don't plant, He said, or harvest, or fill any barns... and your heavenly Father feeds them. <short pause> A bird is busy all day long. <short pause> It simply isn't busy with Thursday. <short pause> Then He said this, in Matthew chapter six, verse thirty-four.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: In that older English, taking thought meant worrying, being pulled apart by care. <short pause> He isn't telling you never to plan. <short pause> He is honest that each day has trouble of its own. <short pause> He just won't let you carry two days' trouble on one day's bread.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: So let's give today some edges. <short pause> With one finger, on your leg or in the palm of your hand, draw a small square. <short pause> Four sides. <short pause> Slowly. <short pause> That square is today. <short pause> It starts where you woke, and it ends where you next lie down to rest. <short pause> Nothing else has to fit inside it.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: Now, what truly belongs in the square? <short pause> Look at your worry, and find the piece of it that can be done today. <short pause> One call. One form. One meal, one kindness, one honest rest. <short pause> Set that piece inside. <short pause> If there is no piece at all for today... then the square is allowed to be empty.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: And the rest of it, set outside the line. <short pause> The answer you don't have. <short pause> The day you are dreading. <short pause> All the what ifs. <short pause> You aren't throwing them away. <short pause> You are leaving them in tomorrow, which is where they live... <short pause> and where God already is.

parts.style: tender reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: I can't promise you that tomorrow will be easy, and neither does this verse. <short pause> It promises a Father who knows what you need. <short pause> When that day becomes a today, it will have its own square, and its own bread. <short pause> You will not arrive there before Him.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Here is our fourth step, joined to the others. <short pause> Palms up... here it is. <short pause> Shoulders down... it's Yours. <short pause> Hand on your heart... help me, and thank You. <short pause> And then the little square, drawn with one finger... <short pause> just today.

parts.style: prayerful, slow, soft but clearly spoken
parts.text: Let's pray. <short pause> Our Father, give me this day my daily bread, and the grace to eat it without staring at tomorrow's plate. <short pause> Show me the piece that is mine to do. <short pause> Watch over everything outside the line. <short pause> And meet me in the next day, when it comes. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: warm, steady, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: As you go, when your thoughts run on ahead, you don't have to chase them. <short pause> Draw the square. <short pause> On a table, on the steering wheel when you've parked, in the pocket of your coat. <short pause> And tell your busy heart, very kindly... <short pause> just today.
